title: Phrases
goal: Two common words can share one stroke when their keys do not collide. It is a real two-to-one saving.

blocks.x: *of* is [[of|-F]] and *the* is [[the|-T]]. They share no key, so pressing both at once, [[of the|-FT]], is a stroke nothing else uses. That makes *of the* one stroke instead of two. It is the commonest word pair in the language.
A phrase is the **union of the keys** of the two words' own strokes. If you know the two words, you can work the phrase out; if the keys would collide, no phrase exists.
Striking the two words one after the other still works. The phrase stroke is only a faster way in, so you can adopt phrases one at a time.
Some phrases are the first stroke of a longer word with a word fused in: *implications of* is [[implications of|*EUFP/+KAEUGSZ]]. Those are pure bonuses; learn the two-word ones first.
